sections.label: Motion inspired by former education Ministers
sections.summary: The Motion is inspired by two 4G former education Ministers, Ng Chee Meng and Heng Swee Keat.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Indeed, Mr Speaker, the Motion I propose and that is seconded and supported by my eight Nominated Member of Parliament (NMP) colleagues and four other elected Members of Parliament, is, indeed, inspired by two fourth-generation (4G) former education Ministers: first, Mr Ng Chee Meng who encouraged the NMPs to consider how a love for learning should be instilled within the education system, especially in the formative preschool years; and second, Mr Heng Swee Keat whom many educators, even today, look up to for his path-breaking choices and ideas.

sections.label: Humanities education and PSLE question
sections.summary: Mr Kok Heng Leun will suggest promoting humanities education and ask whether the PSLE should be done away with.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Kok Heng Leun will suggest how humanities education should be promoted and ask a controversial question: is it time to do away with the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE)?

sections.label: Tuition advertisements promising results
sections.summary: These ads promise incredible results, like an A-star Chinese average in 24 hours, and are insidious.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But these ads, much like slimming pill advertisements, promise incredible results and are equally insidious.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They suggest, in one example, that an A-star average in Chinese can be secured in just 24 hours, if you choose that particular agency.

sections.label: Regulating tuition advertisements and grade preoccupation
sections.summary: The speaker says such tuition ads should be regulated and asks the Ministry what else it plans to do.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I ask myself, "Should this be the way that tuition for primary schools, 10-year-olds is advertised, saying that you will get results, but for a price?" Forget the process; forget the love for learning a subject through dedicated guidance, peer support and patience.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These advertisements and the tuition agencies that produce and disseminate them should with respect, Mr Speaker, be regulated.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Not only because they may be false and misleading, but because they promote gaming the education system.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They extol quick solutions and well-to-do parents will fork out the cash for these quick solutions.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Studies show that excessive tuition can harm rather than help a child and, yes, parents and children should be cautioned and counselled, but the preoccupation with grades must change, Mr Speaker, and I invite the Ministry to indicate what else it plans to do, going forward, on its part.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As Minister Ong Ye Kung revealed at the Committee of Supply Debates: students from Singapore have consistently come up tops in the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) and Trends in International Math and Science Study (TIMSS) rankings for decades.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We did very well this year as well.

sections.label: Top schools and social mobility
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to invite top secondary schools to account for ensuring social mobility is not frustrated.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Might I ask the Ministry to invite other top secondary schools that I have just mentioned, to also account what they are doing to ensure that social mobility is never frustrated and that elite groups of Singaporeans and foreigners in these schools who emerge do not only look out for their own.

sections.label: Asia-literacy in education system
sections.summary: The question asks what Singapore is doing at primary and secondary levels to ensure students are Asia-literate.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When that is the reality, for Australia, which started this idea 10 years ago, what precisely are we doing within our education system, at the primary and secondary school levels, to ensure that our students are Asia-literate?

sections.label: Asia-literate students in schools
sections.summary: The speaker urges secondary schools, JCs, IHLs and universities to make students Asia-literate, distilling initiatives like One-Belt-One-Road and CPTPP for them.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With our advantages as a leading Southeast Asian nation, with clear interests in cross-border trade and investment, I urge that we ensure that secondary schools, junior colleges (JCs), IHLs and the universities contribute to the school of ensuring that our students and our future are Asia-literate.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When we talk about the One-Belt-One-Road initiative, when we talk about the CPTPP, this should be, in some way, at the secondary school or JC level, be reduced, distilled and imparted to students.

sections.label: NCSS disability attitude study
sections.summary: An NCSS 2015 study of 1,400 citizens and permanent residents found the public viewed persons with disabilities less favourably than those without.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The National Council of Social Service (NCSS) conducted an attitude study with 1,400 citizens and permanent residents in 2015 and found that the public viewed persons with disabilities less favourably than those without a disability.

sections.label: Parents uncomfortable with special needs
sections.summary: Half of the parents polled said they were uncomfortable about their child sitting next to a classmate with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Half of the parents they polled indicated that they were uncomfortable about their child having to sit next to one with special needs in class.

sections.label: Enabling Masterplan timeline
sections.summary: The Government began in 2007 with the First Enabling Masterplan, and a decade later the Third Enabling Masterplan was drafted and is being implemented.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Government started the journey in 2007 when the First Enabling Masterplan (EM1) was drafted and adopted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: A decade later, the Third Enabling Masterplan had been drafted and is currently being implemented.

sections.label: SPED and mainstream school pairing
sections.summary: In 2012 MOE announced 20 Special Education Schools would be paired with mainstream schools so students could mingle at recess and school events.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2012, MOE announced that 20 Special Education (SPED) Schools will be paired with mainstream schools so that students from both schools have the opportunities to mingle, for example, during recess and at school events.

sections.label: Professionals survey on challenges
sections.summary: Of 423 professionals surveyed, 51% cited quick burnout, 44% unattractive salaries and benefits, and 34% manpower shortage as challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Fifty-one percent of the 423 professionals surveyed felt that burning out quickly was one of the key challenges they faced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Forty-four percent said salaries and benefits were unattractive while 34% pointed to manpower shortage as a challenge.

sections.label: Special education teachers' pay and status
sections.summary: A proposal that special education teachers come under MOE to access the same salary scales and career opportunities as mainstream peers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The general perception is that these teachers receive less recognition and their pay packages are less attractive than their counterparts in mainstream education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I propose that these teachers come under the purview of MOE, like their peers in mainstream schools, so that they would have access to the same salary scales, as well as career opportunities, which would, in turn, raise the stature and attractiveness of the role and encourage more to pursue a career in this profession.

sections.label: MOE Psychologist Partnership Programme proposal
sections.summary: A proposal for an MOE Psychologist Partnership Programme where recognised private psychologists provide learning difficulty assessments, with CHAS subsidies for families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Taking a leaf from the General Practitioners (GP)-Partnership Programme in the mental health sector, I propose an MOE Psychologist Partnership Programme where several recognised private psychologists can provide assessments for learning difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: To address high costs, the identified practitioners could provide subsidies to families with the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) cards, with part of the costs subsidised by the Government.

sections.label: Special needs children and curriculum
sections.summary: Children with special needs in mainstream schools are still expected to complete the same curriculum as their peers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: For example, at the moment, children with special needs in mainstream schools are still expected to complete the same curriculum as their peers.

sections.label: Proposing an amendment to the Motion
sections.summary: A Member seeks the Speaker's permission to propose an amendment to the Motion to give resolution to the matter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, I am of the view that it would be useful to give some resolution to the matter at hand.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Therefore, Mr Speaker, with your permission, may I propose an amendment to the Motion.

sections.label: Inclusive education and proposed amendment
sections.summary: An amendment is proposed to add words on building an education system supporting each student, recognising talent, helping vulnerable families and uniting young Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Developing a good education system that is inclusive and suited to the times should be a constant work-in-progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: I believe our robust discussion today will contribute towards the continued development of a quality education for all children in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: It has been proposed as an amendment, in line 4 after the word "learners", to add the following words: "by building an education system that: (a)  gives each student the best possible support, and the opportunity and motivation to excel; (b)  recognises ability and talent in every student, and offers development paths suited to their unique strengths and interests; (c)  enables Singaporeans to improve our lives, paying special attention to students from vulnerable families; and (d)  becomes a platform to bring our young together, to build an inclusive and united Singapore." It may be convenient that the debate on the Original Motion and on any other amendments moved by Members be proceeded with simultaneously as a debate on a single question.

sections.label: Questions on young Singaporeans' identity
sections.summary: Two questions were asked about young Singaporeans' uncertainty and indifference, and General Paper tuition was experimented with as a strategic medium.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The first was: "Why are so many young Singaporeans graduating out of our local education system uncertain about who they are and indifferent to bigger problems in Singapore and the world?" And the second question was: "What can we do about it?" We experimented with General Paper tuition as a strategic medium to help 18-year-olds consider their individual and collective responsibilities and we found that if you help kids get curious about who they are and what they care about, they get naturally more curious about how their individual choices connect with broader systemic issues.

sections.label: Medical student quitting profession
sections.summary: A medical team emphasised empathy after a student said she was quitting over surgeons' derogatory comments about an unconscious patient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One medical team shared with us that their conviction to put more emphasis on empathy in their curriculum came after a disillusioned medical student revealed to them that she was quitting the profession after she witnessed two surgeons she was supposed to be learning from execute a surgical procedure with flawless expertise, while simultaneously making the most vile and derogatory comments about the unconscious patient.

sections.label: Educators' wish list of support
sections.summary: Educators' recurring wishes are more time for teaching and learning, smaller classes, and abolishing high-stakes exams, with over-stuffed calendars.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When I talk to educators, three big things recur on their wish list of what “best possible support” could look like: (a) more time to focus on teaching and learning; (b) reduction in class sizes; and (c) abolishing the high-stakes exams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: All teachers who take their work seriously will tell you that school calendars are over-stuffed and it is a constant struggle to claw back time to just focus on teaching.

sections.label: Singapore class sizes versus OECD
sections.summary: Primary and secondary classes average 33 to 34 students, and Primary 1 and 2 average 29, above OECD averages of 21 and 24.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Right now, our primary and secondary schools still average at 33 to 34 students per class.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Primary 1 and 2 average at 29 pupils, which is still way above the average Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) primary and secondary class sizes 21 and 24.

sections.label: Adjusting class sizes amid declining births
sections.summary: Declining birth rates and school closures offer a chance to adjust class sizes to address teachers' longstanding concerns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With declining birth rates and schools closing, we can take the opportunity to adjust our class sizes to a more sustainable number to address some of our teachers' longstanding concerns.

sections.label: Smaller classes trial suggestion
sections.summary: Smaller class sizes are a huge investment, and the passage asks why not take up Leon Perera's 2017 suggestion of a small trial.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Having smaller class sizes across the system is a very huge investment but if it would allow teachers more time and space to train learners in thinking, then it is a luxury worth investing in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, why not take up Non-Constituency Member of Parliament Leon Perera's suggestion in 2017, that MOE consider conducting a small trial to find out if reduced sizes could improve students' results?

sections.label: Exam preparation consuming school term
sections.summary: A teacher wanting to do anything interesting has only four weeks a term, as 40% of the term goes to exam preparation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Which means if the teacher wants to do anything interesting, he only has four weeks in a term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, 40% of the school term is taken up by exam preparation.

sections.label: Tuition industry business models
sections.summary: The billion-dollar tuition industry is still not pivoting its business models to help kids grow in character rather than grades.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The billion-dollar tuition industry is still not pivoting their business models to help kids grow in character rather than in grades any time soon.

sections.label: Abolishing PSLE teething issues
sections.summary: Abolishing PSLE someday would take a painful decade to iron out teething issues before reaching a steady state with fewer difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we do abolish PSLE someday, these teething issues would take probably a painful decade to iron out, but once a steady state is reached, there would be much less difficulties.

sections.label: 16-year-olds and high-stakes exams
sections.summary: A 16-year-old is far more cognitively prepared to deal with the psychological impact of a high-stakes exam than a 12-year-old.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Moreover, I think a 16-year-old is far more cognitively prepared to deal with the psychological impact of a high-stakes exam than a 12-year-old.

sections.label: Achievement file visual artefacts
sections.summary: The file contains rich visual artefacts like photos of key moments or outstanding work that help everyone appreciate a child's progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The file contains very rich visual artefacts like photos of key moments or outstanding pieces of work that help everyone appreciate how far their child has come.

sections.label: Co-created achievement file and principal rotation
sections.summary: The achievement file's message was that the parent was part of the child's growth, and parents raised that principals rotate in five- to six-year cycles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That message sent by the achievement file was compassionate but very clear: I, the parent, was part of the process of my child's growth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This co-created achievement file, while much more costly in investment of time, can change the relationship between parents and teacher from an adversarial, consumeristic one to a collaborative and empathetic one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The second thing that parents raised was how principals were rotated in five- to six-year cycles, preventing neighbourhood schools from deepening their commitment to a unique set of strengths and interests.

sections.label: ReadAble classes reading outcomes
sections.summary: Kids who attended ReadAble classes regularly before age six started reading at Primary 1 or above grade level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: All the kids who started attending these ReadAble classes regularly before the age of six actually started reading at Primary 1 or above grade level.

sections.label: Northlight school for PSLE failures
sections.summary: Northlight is a school for kids who failed PSLE or dropped out, floated in 1997 and made real in 2005.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And, no, this is not a school for the elite; this is just the opposite.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is a school designed to support kids who failed PSLE two or three times, as well as those who dropped out of the system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This school is Northlight and it was an idea floated in 1997 and dismissed as before its time and made real only in 2005 when Mr Lim Chuan Poh, a Permanent Secretary at MOE, had the curiosity to find an answer to one student's frustration about why he had to repeat PSLE so many times.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That Permanent Secretary's leap of faith allowed more leaders and purpose-driven principals and teachers to come and put their own skin in the game and it was all of them combined together – their collective courage to live out their highest ideals of education that made Northlight happen.

sections.label: Call for Education Masterplan
sections.summary: Northlight's model offers lessons for mainstream schools, and the speaker calls for an Education Masterplan for the Future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Northlight's model contains so many wisdoms and insights that mainstream schools can learn from and it is a beautiful symbol of what is possible if we care enough to make things happen not just for ourselves but for others who we do not want to leave behind.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I want to make a call for an Education Masterplan for the Future – a masterplan to be jointly developed by Government and other key stakeholder groups; a masterplan to span over the life stages of a learner, from cradle to the third age; and a masterplan to be reviewed every three years.

sections.label: Need for holistic education masterplan
sections.summary: A changing world needs a consolidated education masterplan with shared vision and self-motivated learners who master technology.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: With the world changing so exponentially, we will need a more consolidated and holistic education masterplan for the future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We need an education masterplan that is not as disjointed and that can articulate the overall vision, values, principles, learning approaches and roles of different partners; a plan to develop self-motivated learners from young to old holistically, with a strong passion for learning, comfortable with discomfort and even disruptions; who are not slaves and consumers of technology but masters and even creators of technology.

sections.label: Singapore as tuition nation
sections.summary: The speaker states that Singapore continues to be a tuition nation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Indeed, we continue to be a "tuition nation".

sections.label: Tuition for well-performing children
sections.summary: Seventy-two percent of surveyed parents who send children for tuition do so when the children already perform well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Seventy-two percent of parents surveyed who send their children for tuition do so when their children are already performing well in school.

sections.label: Masterplan to collect the dots
sections.summary: Because lifelong education is complicated, an overall education masterplan is needed to collect and join the dots.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The world of lifelong education is complicated and no one knows it all.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And this is the reason why we need an overall education masterplan for the future to collect the dots, to join the dots, so that it makes sense for everyone; so that we know where we are heading; and what each of us has to do.

sections.label: Hiring for skills over qualifications
sections.summary: Employers and industry captains must hone skills mastery and hire for skills rather than using paper qualifications and academic scores as hiring proxies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Employers and industry captains must be active in honing skills mastery and hire for skills and stop using paper qualifications and academic scores as proxies for hiring criteria.

sections.label: Education Master Plan for the Future
sections.summary: Citing eliminated football teams, the speaker calls for a joint Education Master Plan for the Future so Singapore charts its own path in education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Many of us have watched – I do not watch football much but my husband updates me a lot on this and he watches with his friends, in disbelief and dismay how prestigious favourite teams, such as Germany, Brazil, Argentina and Spain, have all been eliminated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We are reminded that past success is no guarantee of current or future success.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Hence, I call again for the joint development of an Education Master Plan for the Future to consolidate all that we have done across the life stages of learners; to retain the best and boldly slaughter the sacred cows which serve us no longer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Singapore should chart our own path of significance, not just success, in education; march to the beats of our own hearts and drum; and take the path less travelled if that is the one we need.

sections.label: Worries over technology and inequality
sections.summary: Technological advances, rising ideological and sectorial conflicts, and unchecked capitalism and consumerism are causes for worry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Technological advances have given cause for worry, in terms of economic disruptions and adverse effects on human interactions and interpersonal relations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Ideological and sectorial conflicts are on the rise, leading to confrontations, polarisation and violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Rampant capitalism and consumerism, left unchecked, are also widening the inequality gap in our society.

sections.label: Facebook group accusing The Esplanade
sections.summary: The speaker cites a Facebook group accusing The Esplanade of promoting bestiality over an artwork by Vincent Leow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is you versus me, us versus them, my truth versus yours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am reminded of the recent incident of a group of people organised under a Facebook group accusing The Esplanade of "promoting bestiality" when the latter displayed an artwork of Singapore artist Vincent Leow at the Community Walk on the third level of The Esplanade.

sections.label: Deepening humanities study in education
sections.summary: The speaker appeals to MOE to deepen its efforts to ensure the humanities are studied deeply and widely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As such, I appeal to MOE to deepen its efforts in ensuring that the humanities are studied deeply and widely.

sections.label: Education system preoccupied with quick results
sections.summary: The education system is so preoccupied with quick results that little time is permitted for holistic growth and exploration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, our education system is so preoccupied with quick results that there is little time permitted for such holistic growth and exploration.

sections.label: Collaboration over competition for nation
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether Singapore should harness collective capabilities through collaboration instead of competition, which creates silos and alienation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Like it or not, competition creates silos and alienation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We are a small nation of 5.6 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How about harnessing our collective capabilities instead through collaboration, so that we, as a nation, can move mountains at no one's expense?

sections.label: Theatre-making and abolishing PSLE
sections.summary: The speaker calls theatre-making an alternative schooling model and says the sacred cow of the PSLE should be seriously considered for slaughter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I always think that theatre-making is an alternative schooling model.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We should seriously consider slaughtering this sacred cow of the PSLE.

sections.label: Support for masterplan suggestion
sections.summary: The speaker supports Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng's masterplan suggestion, saying it should cover classroom sizes, assessment models and teacher capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With that, I really support fellow Member, Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng, for her suggestion on the masterplan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This masterplan should include looking at classroom sizes, assessment models and the capacity of teachers.

sections.label: Assessment focuses on quantity not quality
sections.summary: The speaker states that assessment methods today focus on the quantity students have learnt rather than the quality of their learning and retention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yet today our assessment methods are still focused on the quantity that students have learnt, rather than the quality of their learning and retention.

sections.label: Shift in assessment thinking
sections.summary: The speaker says adopting a fundamental shift in thinking about assessment will change how lessons are taught and how learning journeys are scaffolded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we adopt this fundamental shift in thinking about assessment, it will change how lessons are being taught and, subsequently, how individual learning journeys can be scaffolded.

sections.label: More space for teachers
sections.summary: The speaker says the runway for teachers to adopt new approaches is too short, so teachers need more space to learn and experiment, including relief from administrative duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, while these new approaches, taken on to alleviate pressure and produce more well-rounded students, are beneficial, the runway for teachers to adopt them and produce the same results is simply too short.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I think we need to give more space for teachers to learn and experiment, and a way to do this is to relief them of their administrative duties.

sections.label: Parental work and teacher stress
sections.summary: The passage asks whether parents' focus on work reduces time with children and makes them a source of stress for teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In our bid to make a living, to ensure that we best provide for our children materially, have we become so caught up with work that there is a trade-off in our time spent with them?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In doing so, have we become the source of stress for teachers, constantly checking on them, harrassing them, being critics of them and as if we know better and can tell teachers how to teach the children better?

sections.label: Teachers as equals, not salespersons
sections.summary: The passage says teachers work with parents, not for them, and expresses thanks for a Motion seeking an education system revamp.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: Teachers have a job to fulfil to the best of their capabilities and that is true.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: So, do not treat teachers like you are a customer, that they are salespersons at your beck and call.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: Rather, see them as equals, because that is what they are trying to do: to work with you and not for you, all for the benefit of your child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: There is room for change and collaboration and that is why I am so deeply thankful for this Motion so that we can take in all these thoughts and ideas and hope that the Government will seriously consider making a huge revamp of our education system.

sections.label: Tuition and grade worry surveys
sections.summary: A survey found four in 10 Singapore families send preschool children to tuition, and 86% of Singapore students worried about poor grades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A survey found that four in 10 families in Singapore now send their preschool children to tuition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The most common reason for tuition, cited by more than half of the parents with children under seven, was to keep up with others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: According to a survey, 66% of students across all OECD countries said they were worried about poor grades at school, but among Singapore students, it was 86%.

sections.label: Shift early education to holistic growth
sections.summary: The passage proposes shifting early education from linear academic emphasis to holistic growth, with Government controlling two-thirds of the industry by 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One way to do this is to shift early education away from a linear academic emphasis, to a more rounded emphasis focusing on holistic growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There are many factors involved here but as around two-thirds of the early childhood education industry will be controlled by the Government by 2023 and with the establishment of the National Institute of Early Childhood Development, the Government can play an important role here.

sections.label: Parents want social-emotional learning
sections.summary: A Chapter Zero survey showed parents' top hopes were healthy relationships and emotional health, with 70% wanting more social-emotional learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A survey by Chapter Zero, a social enterprise working with parents, caregivers and educators in Singapore, showed that the top two qualities parents hoped to see for their child were "healthy relationships with others" and "strong emotional health".

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Seventy percent of the parents raised the need for more emphasis on social-emotional learning in preschools and primary schools, particularly on mindfulness, empathy and conflict management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Studies have shown that there is correlation between the level of pro-social behaviour that a student showed in kindergarten and their education and job prospects, criminal activity, likelihood of substance abuse and mental health in adulthood.

sections.label: MOE Enhanced Performance Management System
sections.summary: MOE's Enhanced Performance Management System was instituted in 2005 and reviewed in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MOE's Enhanced Performance Management System (EPMS) was instituted in 2005 and reviewed in 2014.

sections.label: Education pathways and aspirations
sections.summary: The speaker says education is meaningless if pathways lead to a similar destination without achieving dreams, and suggests multiple education systems and strategies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It will be meaningless if the education system merely provides pathways to a similar destination, without achieving one’s dreams and aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to suggest, for consideration, multiple education systems and strategies, so that we can fulfil this aim.

sections.label: Home circumstances affecting students
sections.summary: The speaker gives examples of a student in a cramped shared flat and one caring for a sibling finding study harder than classmates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another example, a student studying in a cramped 2-room flat that is shared with another family might find it a struggle, compared to another who has the luxury of studying in a room of his or her own; or a student who has to stay up late to care for his younger sibling because his mother is working, is likely to find it harder to concentrate in school, compared to his classmate who does not have to.

sections.label: Levelling the playing field
sections.summary: The speaker says hard decisions must be made to level the playing field and mitigate the effects of each child's different circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hard decisions must be made to look at how we can truly make the playing field level for everyone and how we can help mitigate the effects of the different circumstances faced by each child in order to help them succeed in school.

sections.label: Education strategies with a heart
sections.summary: The speaker says that just as society is built with a heart, the education system must develop its strategies with a heart.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just as we work towards building a society and a nation with a heart, our education system has to develop its strategies with a heart.

sections.label: One-size-fits-all education system
sections.summary: The speaker calls the current education system a one-size-fits-all approach with minor tweaks, saying pathways to the same destination are meaningless.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is meaningless when the pathways are simply routes to the same destination as everyone else, but not achieving one's dream and aspiration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I regard our current education system as a "one-size-fits-all" approach, with minor tweaks here and there to cater for the incidentals which are away from the mainstream.

sections.label: Parents and paper chase
sections.summary: The speaker observes that many parents remain unconvinced the paper chase is over and still push children towards degrees and paper qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on my observation, many parents still remain unconvinced that the days of the paper chase are over and that they are still pushing their children to strive towards degrees and paper qualifications.

sections.label: Primary 2 problem-sum models
sections.summary: Primary 2 students are now expected to draw problem-sum models previously reserved for older primary students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, Primary 2 students are now expected to draw problem-sum models when, in the past, these are reserved only for the older primary school students.

sections.label: Standardised tests as obstacle
sections.summary: The need for standardised tests is one big obstacle preventing this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The need for standardised tests is one big obstacle preventing this.

sections.label: Multiple education systems and strategies
sections.summary: The speaker urges considering multiple education systems and strategies away from one-size-fits-all to serve varying individual needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us embolden ourselves to consider multiple education systems and strategies with different approaches, away from the "one-size-fits-all", to serve the varying individual needs, where our dreams and aspirations can become a reality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the right education strategies, I am confident that we will progress as a nation with a heart.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Not only shall we progress as a nation, but also as an integrated society where we truly see our fellow Singaporeans as family.

sections.label: Seven skills for students
sections.summary: The speaker lists seven skills and urges the Government to cultivate making connections and self-directed engaged learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The skills are: focus and control, perspective taking, communications, making connections, critical thinking, willingness to take on challenges and self-directed and engaged learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Among these seven skills, I strongly urge the Government to cultivate making connections and self-directed and engaged learning in our students and youths.

sections.label: Design thinking and macro-worldview
sections.summary: Building these skills requires exposure to concepts like design thinking and oscillating between a macro-worldview and seeing how pieces fit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Building these skills would require our students to be exposed to concepts, such as design thinking and having the ability to oscillate between possessing a macro-worldview and the ability to see how different pieces fit into that view.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would strongly suggest that MOE consider how our youths can be exposed to such concepts from a young age so that they could adopt a more holistic approach in dealing with the complex challenges of the future.

sections.label: Tuition for struggling students
sections.summary: Students weak or struggling should have opportunity for tuition, with self-help groups and community organisations providing affordable tuition to needy students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But we should also step back and take a look at it from the perspective of times when students do need additional help if they are weak in their subjects, if they are struggling, for them to be able to have the opportunity to take tuition in order that they may actually improve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And while I take the point also that parents who perhaps have the means to afford tuition of a different level would be able to pay for that tuition, we also do have self-help groups and community organisations that are able to provide tuition to needy students, to needy families for students who need help at affordable rates.

sections.label: PSLE cram-and-deliver assessment
sections.summary: Speaker suggests MOE make PSLE reflect other skill sets, perhaps through coursework or continuous assessment, without scrapping the exam.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Ultimately, a good PSLE T-score demonstrates a child’s ability to cram for exams and deliver in a controlled exam-based environment and one wonders if that is an accurate reflection of his or her potential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, while I am not advocating the scrapping of the PSLE and I acknowledge the proposed changes being made to this exam by MOE, I would like to suggest that MOE consider how it can make the PSLE more about a demonstration of other skill sets and capabilities, other than the ability to “cram-and-deliver.” Perhaps, the element of coursework or continuous assessment could be introduced as part of one’s PSLE grade, such that the eventual PSLE score is a more holistic reflection of a young adult’s capabilities and abilities.

sections.label: Primary school curriculum diversity
sections.summary: Speaker notes primary education follows a one-size-fits-all centrally planned curriculum and urges MOE to run pilot programmes for diverse curricula.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While multiple options are provided for pre- and post-primary school students, the primary education sector still follows a one-size-fits-all model where schools administer a centrally planned curriculum with limited room for variations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As evidenced by how our post-primary and tertiary education sectors have produced a varied pool of talent who are skilled in a variety of different fields, could we not also allow our primary schools to be more diverse in offering their own curriculum that caters to different learning needs and aspirations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Diversity ultimately results in a whole that is always more than the sum of its parts and I would like to encourage MOE to perhaps run some pilot programmes in the primary school sector to see how alternate systems and pedagogies could also be successful.

sections.label: Thanking educators for developing people
sections.summary: Speaker says everyone tells teachers how to teach, notes their workload and role shaping young people, and thanks educators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But everybody seems to want to tell teachers and educators how they should teach the children in school, so, it is tough.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We have to deal with the amount of work outside of the classroom.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We have to deal also with the fact that we are shaping and growing young people and young children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, I would like to take this moment just to say "Thank you" to all our educators; whether you are a preschool educator or a professor in a university.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But most of all, thank you for continuing to develop the one resource, the one resource that will always be critical to Singapore’s success and, that is, our people.

sections.label: Online CCA registration limited places
sections.summary: Most schools have online CCA registration opening for a specific window, and limited places mean children may not get the chosen CCA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Most	schools	now	have	an	online	registration	system	for	CCAs that	opens for	a	specific	window,	during	which	parents	must	go	online	to	register	their	child	for the CCA of their choice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And	it is	not	a	given	that	you	will	get	to	play	the	sport	or	CCA	that	you have	selected	for	your	child	as	there	are	limited	places.

sections.label: Schools farm out CCAs to vendors
sections.summary: Speaker understands schools farm out some CCAs to external vendors who cannot cope with large numbers or are not paid to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As	I	understand	it,	part	of	the	reason	for	this	is	that	schools	now	farm	out	some	of	their	CCAs	to	external	vendors	who	cannot	cope	with	the	large	numbers	of	students	keen	on	popular	sports,	or	are	not	paid	to	do	so.

sections.label: Affluent parents engage private coaches
sections.summary: Speaker says more affluent parents engage private coaches while children from less affluent families play alternative sports they may not like.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What	this	means	is	that	the	more	affluent	parents	will	engage	private	coaches	for	their	children, and the children	from	less	affluent	families	make	do	with	playing	an	alternative	sport	which	they	may	not	like	or	have	any	interest	in.

sections.label: Schools pooling resources for CCAs
sections.summary: Schools pooling resources could alleviate cost concerns, since farming out CCAs to vendors usually means parents top up fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Schools	pooling	their	resources	could	also	alleviate	cost	concerns	as, when	CCAs	are	farmed	out	to	vendors,	it	usually	means	that	parents	have	to	top	up the fees.

sections.label: Sports CCA vendor credentials
sections.summary: It asks what the credentials of sports CCA vendors are and how they are assessed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For sports CCAs, what are the credentials of these vendors and how are they assessed?

sections.label: DSA programme and DSA coaches
sections.summary: The 2004 DSA programme guaranteed places to talented Primary 6 and Secondary 4 students, and an unintended consequence is the emergence of DSA coaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When conceived and introduced in 2004, the programme was to enable Primary 6 and Secondary 4 students who are exceptionally talented not just in academics but also CCAs, and sports included, to be guaranteed places in secondary schools or JCs, through tests and trials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One unintended consequence of the scheme is the emergence of "DSA coaches".

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These are sports coaches who have, over the years, studied the DSA entrance requirements of schools and created programmes that aim to guarantee your child a place in the school of choice if you enrol your child in their classes over a period of time.

sections.label: Tweaking DSA trials criteria
sections.summary: It suggests the Ministry could tweak DSA trials to include criteria such as sportsmanship, fair play and values exhibited like Sean See.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Perhaps, the Ministry can work on tweaking the DSA trials to include criteria, such as sportsmanship, fair play and traits and values exhibited like Sean See from St Andrew's Secondary School.

sections.label: Values criteria in DSA selection
sections.summary: Including these criteria in DSA selection would signal the kind of young Singapore it hopes to nurture and create a more level playing field.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By including these other criteria in the DSA selection process, the Ministry would send a strong signal to the teachers, coaches, parents and children about the kind of young Singapore it hopes to nurture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And it will also create a more level playing field as these values cannot be paid for.

sections.label: Understanding children and sport education
sections.summary: Some children cannot adapt to those environments, causing mental health issues, so parents must understand and listen to their children better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But, then, some children won't be able to adapt to those environments and that will cause mental health issues." The point here is that, as parents, we need to understand our children better, to listen more and to listen effectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And as far as sport education is concerned, we would have succeeded when sport elicits the same unbridled joy in every child that we see when the school bell rings to announce it is time for recess.

sections.label: Coaching classes and Direct Schools Admission
sections.summary: Affluent parents send children for coaching classes to enter top schools under Direct Schools Admission, which favours them and discriminates against less well-off parents, so a level playing field is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, affluent parents send their children for multiple coaching classes so that they can get into top schools under the Direct Schools Admission programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This favours the affluent parents and discriminates against the less well-off parents who may not be able to afford such classes to prepare their children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, there needs to be a level playing field.

sections.label: Question on most important teacher
sections.summary: The speaker poses two questions to Members, including who is the most important teacher in a child's life, noting systems, structures and processes are important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Before we resume, can I just perhaps pose two questions to Members: who is the most important teacher in our child's life?

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I think systems, structures, processes are important, but I think it is useful to think about what the answers to those questions might be.

sections.label: Singaporeans using SkillsFuture credits
sections.summary: As of 1 February 2018, 285,000 Singaporeans have used their SkillsFuture credits.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As of 1 February 2018, 285,000 Singaporeans have used their SkillsFuture credits.

sections.label: Singapore education system and literacy
sections.summary: Singapore's education system is highly regarded but stressful, was top-performing in Science, Mathematics and Reading in a 2015 OECD study, and adult literacy rose from 92.5% in 2000 to 96.8% in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore's education system is among the most highly regarded in the world, but it is also a very stressful one for the students and young people.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We were the top-performing country in Science, Mathematics and Reading in a 2015 study by 	the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The adult literacy rate of Singapore increased from 92.5% in 2000 to 96.8% in 2015 with an annual growth rate of 0.75%.

sections.label: Prime minister without a degree
sections.summary: In his interview with The Straits Times, he said a prime minister without a degree can happen not too far off, as nothing inherent in a Minister's job requires a degree.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In his interview with The Straits Times, he also, with pragmatism, said, "A prime minister without a degree can happen not too far off in the future as there is nothing inherent in a Minister's job that requires a degree".

sections.label: Pathways to success and aptitude-based admissions
sections.summary: There are many pathways to success, and the speaker applauds Minister Ong for introducing aptitude-based admissions and lifelong opportunities in higher education.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are many pathways to achieving success and success is defined as what one sees as success.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: He further said, "Education has been, and will continue to be, an uplifting and integrating force in society." I applaud Minister Ong, being a proponent of an aptitude-based selection process, for his bold move to introduce aptitude-based admissions and lifelong opportunities in an increasingly diverse higher education landscape during his time as Education Minister (Higher Education and Skills).

sections.label: Public Service recruitment revamp
sections.summary: Public Service, Government agencies and Statutory Boards must revamp recruitment to emphasise aptitude, attitude and skills over paper qualification.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For skills to be truly recognised across Singapore, we must ensure Public Service, Government agencies and Statutory Boards revamp its recruitment methods to provide greater emphasis on aptitude, attitude and skills, with less focus on paper qualification.

sections.label: National lifelong learning movement
sections.summary: Lifelong learning is the ongoing, voluntary and self-motivated pursuit of knowledge, and a national lifelong learning movement is needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As defined, lifelong learning is the "ongoing, voluntary and self-motivated" pursuit of knowledge for either personal or professional reasons.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There must be a national lifelong learning movement across Singapore.

sections.label: Mindset change for skills recognition
sections.summary: Mindset change is the important ingredient for recognising skills and aptitudes instead of paper qualification.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mindset change is the important ingredient to the recipe of recognising skills and aptitudes, instead of paper qualification.

sections.label: Inclusive education commitment
sections.summary: Singapore's accession to UN conventions shows commitment to inclusive education, with SPED and mainstream school resourcing and compulsory education from 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore's accession to the United Nations (UN) Convention on the Rights of the Child and the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities is testament to our country’s commitment to provide an inclusive education for all children and youth, including those with disabilities and special needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This commitment is shown in the Government's resourcing of special education (SPED) schools and mainstream schools to support students with special needs and disabilities and the implementation of compulsory education for children with disabilities and special needs with effect from 2019.

sections.label: Inclusive education academic progress
sections.summary: Studies show children undergoing inclusive education achieve greater progress in reading, Mathematics and general academic performance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In respect of the first principle, studies show that children undergoing inclusive education achieve greater progress in reading, Mathematics and general academic performance.

sections.label: Support services for students with disabilities
sections.summary: Professional support services should be accessible on a continuing, sustained and sustainable basis, with MOH, MOE and MSF reviewing support and funding structures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To increase the level of independence of students with disabilities or special needs, the suite of professional support services, on whatever basis, should be accessible to students on a continuing, sustained and sustainable basis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I, therefore, propose that the Ministry of Health (MOH), MOE and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) collaboratively review the support and funding structures accordingly.

sections.label: Mayflower Primary School deaf students
sections.summary: Mayflower Primary School enrolled six deaf students this year and made systemic and infrastructural changes to accommodate them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Closer to home, Mayflower Primary School enrolled six deaf students this year and it undertook systemic and infrastructural changes to accommodate them.

sections.label: Inclusive education survey findings
sections.summary: Surveys found seven in 10 Singaporeans support inclusive education, but only half of parents were comfortable with their child sitting next to a disabled child.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on the survey results of the Lien Foundation Inclusive Attitudes Survey in 2016 and the findings from a series of surveys in 2016 by the National Council of Social Service, although seven out of 10 Singaporeans support inclusive education, only half of the parents surveyed are comfortable to let their children sit next to a child with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on the same survey findings, half of the children with special needs had difficulty enrolling in mainstream preschools because of their special needs.

sections.label: Most important teacher and school
sections.summary: The speaker asks who is the most important teacher and school, and says teachers accommodated his disability but treated him the same.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The first: who is the most important teacher in our lives, and which is the most important school?

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am blessed to say that I have had many teachers who made that difference because they did not treat me as inferior to a child without disability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They accommodated my disability but they treated me the same.

sections.label: Growing up together with friends
sections.summary: The speaker says friends may have found him a nuisance, but they grew up together and stuck together.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am sure there were many times my friends felt like I was a nuisance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But you know what, we grew up together.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We did not think we had a choice, we stuck together and we grew up together.

sections.label: Mainstream education for every child
sections.summary: The speaker urges Members to work together for every child, saying mainstream education is an opportunity every child should get.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Ms Chia Yong Yong, like any other Member of Parliament, you have to wrap up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: And I want to say this: that mainstream education, Sir, what I went through is what I think is an opportunity we should give to every child.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: I urge all Members to do and to work together for every child because every child matters.

sections.label: Polytechnic and ITE graduate disparity
sections.summary: The pattern repeats when comparing polytechnic and ITE graduates, but both ratios dipped from 2007 to 2017, narrowing the disparity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The pattern is repeated when you compare polytechnic graduates and their Institute of Technical Education (ITE) counterparts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, both ratios have dipped from 2007 to 2017, indicating that disparity between the different levels of tertiary institution graduates has actually narrowed.

sections.label: Graduate starting salary growth rates
sections.summary: From 2007 to 2017, median gross monthly starting salaries grew 2.1% for graduates, 2.2% for post-NS polytechnic graduates and 4.1% for post-NS ITE graduates.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From 2007 to 2017, the median gross monthly starting salary of graduates in full-time permanent employment grew at a compound annual growth rate of 2.1%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The corresponding figure for post-NS polytechnic graduates is almost the same at 2.2%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For post-NS graduates from ITE, however, the growth was nearly twice this during that period, at 4.1%.

sections.label: Short shelf life of skills
sections.summary: Because the shelf life of skills and learning is short, a sound education system should lay foundations for continuous learning.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Tay’s emphasis and those of the other hon Members I had cited above should lead us to realise that the shelf life of skills and learning has always been short and is possibly getting even shorter in some fields.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Because this shelf life is not much longer than the education and training which had led to their acquisition in the first place, an important objective of a sound education system should be to lay the foundations for a continuous process of learning.

sections.label: Continuing education and lifelong learning
sections.summary: Continuing education and lifelong learning must be as relevant to the economy as early basic education, and the education system must serve lifelong learners with the same rigour.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The imperative for continuing education and lifelong learning to be relevant to the needs of the economy is at least as urgent as it is for early basic education.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our education system must meet the needs of lifelong learners and skills upgraders with the same rigour that it has cemented the basic educational foundation of early learners.

sections.label: Singapore-based professional markers for humanities
sections.summary: One way is to build up a team of Singapore-based professional markers for humanities subjects while continuing to work with Cambridge as examination partner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One way of doing so is to build up a team of Singapore-based professional markers for humanities subjects, even as we continue to work with Cambridge as our examination partner.

sections.label: Curriculum set years before assessment
sections.summary: Even for applied subjects, the curriculum is set two to three years before assessment and lasts four to six years before review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Currently, even for applied subjects, I was told that the curriculum is set two to three years before the actual year of assessment and the curriculum will last for four to six years before review.

sections.label: Hong Kong industry accreditation example
sections.summary: Hong Kong's examination board works with the private sector to accredit industry members to evaluate students, such as auto repair students evaluated by accredited mechanics in real workshops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Rather, I am suggesting we take a look at how Hong Kong's examination board works with the private sector to accredit certain members of the relevant industries to evaluate students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
